message.content:
I can help with nearly all parts of academic research organization and discovery inside this workspace. Short summary of key capabilities:

- Search and import papers
  - Search arXiv for relevant papers by topic or query.
  - Ingest/import arXiv papers (by arXiv ID) into your workspace so they can be searched, indexed, and attached to projects.

- Manage projects and documents
  - Create, list, and reuse research projects (folders).
  - Add imported documents to projects and list project documents.
  - Create markdown notes inside projects.

- Summarize and explore content
  - Summarize specific documents.
  - Search your indexed documents (by title or content).
  - Search a built knowledge graph of entities and relationships in your corpus.

- Workflow-aware actions
  - I follow a safe workflow for adding papers to projects (search → ingest → add).
  - I reuse recent project/document context so you don’t need to supply IDs repeatedly.
  - If you ask to “try again,” I re-run the last tool call with the same arguments.

- Project and result honesty
  - I report tool outcomes exactly (IDs, errors, or empty results).
  - I won’t claim creation/imports unless the tool returned success and I’ll show the IDs when available.

- Research assistance
  - Help find related work, create reading lists, write short summaries or syntheses, prepare literature-review outlines, extract key methods/results, and suggest next experiments or citations.

- Integration details & limits
  - I use arXiv searches and arXiv IDs for ingestion.
  - I can’t invent project/document IDs; I use the system’s IDs returned by tools.
  - If you ask which model I’m running on: this session is routed via Azure deployment model-router, so the underlying model is selected per request and isn’t directly visible here.

Tell me what you want to do next — e.g., create a project, search arXiv for papers on a topic, import specific arXiv IDs, or summarize a document you’ve already added.
